building.name: 2021 South Carolina Building Code (2021 International Building Code with South Carolina modifications)
building.local_amendments_note: South Carolina cities must enforce the state codes, and a local change is valid only if the Building Codes Council approves it. The Council's 2021 and 2024 modification indexes list no modification proposed by the City of Charleston to the building or plumbing code (the only Charleston entries are Charleston Fire Department changes to the fire code, which apply statewide). The state's adoption leaves administrative provisions (permits, fees, appeals) to each city's own ordinance: Charleston's are in Chapter 7 of the City Code, which could not be read (the code library returned HTTP 403).

building.quote: [Building Inspections page] Current Codes: Access to Current South Carolina Codes; 2009 International Energy Conservation Code; 2020 National Electrical Code (NFPA 70); 2021 South Carolina Building Code; 2021 International Existing Building Code; 2021 South Carolina Fuel Gas Code; 2021 South Carolina Fire Code; 2021 South Carolina Mechanical Code; 2021 South Carolina Plumbing Code; 2021 South Carolina Residential Code; 2021 International Swimming Pool and Spa Code; 2017 ICC A117.1 Accessible and Usable Buildings and Facilities (Effective June 1, 2017). scheduled_change.what: The 2024 South Carolina Building Code and 2024 South Carolina Plumbing Code (2024 International codes with South Carolina modifications) replace the 2021 editions. The City's Building Inspections and Permit Center pages both announce the date; City inspectors and plan reviewers attended 2024 code training on November 23 and 24, 2026. The City had not published, on the pages read, the cut-off for applications filed around the change (in 2023 it went by the date a project was submitted for permit). Also on January 1, 2027: Department of Development Services fee increases.
scheduled_change.quote: [Building Inspections page] South Carolina will begin enforcing the 2024 South Carolina Building Codes beginning January 1, 2027. [Permit Center page] Inspectors are attending mandatory 2024 code update trainings in preparation for the new codes to go into effect on January 1, 2027. [...] Department of Development Services fee increases will be effective January 1, 2027. [State notice] The Council established the implementation date for local jurisdictions as January 1, 2027.

fixtures.city_amends_note: Charleston enforces the state's toilet-count table and rules as they stand. The state notice says local modifications not approved by the Building Codes Council are invalid, and the Council's 2021 and 2024 modification indexes carry no Charleston modification to Chapter 29 of the building code or Chapter 4 of the plumbing code. Local detail: when a business applies for a certificate of occupancy, the Building Inspections Division checks the minimum number of restroom fixtures and assigns the maximum occupant load.
fixtures.local_practice_quote: Building Inspections: Verifies the proposed occupied space has the required life-safety means of egress and minimum number of required restroom plumbing fixtures. Assigns the maximum occupant load for the space.
fixtures.state_rule_quote: Only the modifications approved and listed on the Council's website are valid for use in the State. Building code modifications that have not been approved by the Council are invalid and cannot be adopted, employed or enforced by municipalities and counties.

permit.exempt_list_quote: No City of Charleston list of work exempt from a permit was found on charleston-sc.gov, and the City Code (Chapter 7, building permits at Sec. 7-171 and following per a City index) could not be read. What the City's own pages say: [Substantial Improvement and Substantial Damage Regulations in the Special Flood Hazard Area] Substantial Improvement and floodplain regulations apply for existing buildings in the Special Flood Hazard Area (SFHA), Flood Zones AE and VE, as designated by the effective Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM). Please be advised that all work on an existing structure in the SFHA requires a permit, including repairs of storm damage, replacement of HVAC ductwork and non-structural interior renovations. [General Permitting Guidance, Commercial Alteration, September 2025] Permit Type(s) and Work Class(es): "Building Commercial" - "Alteration". Commonly submitted as "Interior renovation" or "Interior/exterior renovation". [...] Required Documents for Permit Application: No floor plan changes: City of Charleston Commercial Alteration/Addition Application; Itemized scope/contract (if scope is vague); MEPG cut sheets if in scope; Photos of existing conditions. [State position, 2024 Code Adoption Notice] Adoption of the mandatory codes does not include the chapters, sections or provisions addressing administrative policies or procedures. Administrative policies and procedures are the sole responsibility of each local jurisdiction. If the governing body of a local jurisdiction desires to use the administrative provisions in one or more of the adopted codes, it must first adopt the chapters or sections by ordinance. [Model list, 2021 South Carolina Building Code Section 105.2 as printed on UpCodes; it applies in Charleston only if the City adopted it by ordinance, which was not confirmed] Permits shall not be required for the following: Building: [...] Painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work. [...] Nonfixed and movable fixtures, cases, racks, counters and partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches (1753 mm) in height.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Charleston job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the South Carolina rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Charleston hotels, restaurants, hospitals and port warehouses, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** South Carolina sets the number of toilets by how many people use the building, and Charleston enforces the state's numbers without changes of its own. The table below shows what that means.
extra_rule_bullets: - **New rules on January 1, 2027:** South Carolina moves to newer editions of its building and plumbing rules that day, and Charleston enforces them from then. The toilet numbers for offices, restaurants and schools and the fire test for solid plastic partitions stay the same. If your permit application falls close to that date, ask the City of Charleston Permit Center which edition applies.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** South Carolina leaves permit procedures to each city. Charleston's commercial alteration permit covers interior renovations, including ones with no floor plan changes. In the city's flood zones (AE and VE on the flood map), the City says all work on an existing building needs a permit, non-structural interior renovations included. None of the City's permit pages names toilet partitions, so ask the City of Charleston Permit Center (843-577-5550) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the City of Charleston Permit Center
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, South Carolina's building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. When a business applies for its certificate of occupancy, Charleston's Building Inspections Division assigns the maximum number of people for the space and checks that it has enough toilets.
page.install_rule: Charleston has no contractor license of its own. For a commercial alteration permit the City asks for two things from the contractor: a City of Charleston business license and a South Carolina contractor license. South Carolina requires a state contractor license when a commercial project's total construction cost is over $10,000. Confirm what your project needs with the City of Charleston Permit Center. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: On a permitted job in Charleston the contractor needs a City business license and a South Carolina contractor license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** South Carolina has no state wage law for public construction, so a set wage applies only on federally funded jobs, under the federal Davis-Bacon Act. For a carpenter on building work in Charleston County that federal rate is $16.03 an hour plus $1.16 in benefits, a figure taken from a 2011 wage survey.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 9% in Charleston: 6% state plus 3% in Charleston County taxes, which are 1% local option, 1% for school buildings and the rest for transportation. The part of the city in Berkeley County is also at 9%.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hotels, hospitals and port buildings:** phenolic or stainless steel where restrooms are cleaned many times a day, HDPE or phenolic where the room is open to outside air.
